subject.title: feat(gateway): add deferred activation control port

question: Should deferred activation be a permanent OpenClaw core protocol, or should Lobster own the control listener and exec the canonical Gateway only after hydration?
rationale: The patch intentionally parks only a control process and makes no preload or performance claim, so the same state-free boundary appears implementable outside core; maintainer intent is needed to decide whether stable process identity or another demonstrated constraint justifies the new environment and HTTP contract.

options.title: Keep orchestration external
options.body: Have Lobster own the loopback activation listener and exec `openclaw gateway` after hydration, avoiding a permanent core protocol until a missing core capability is proven.

options.title: Sponsor the core protocol
options.body: Accept the primitive only after the integration demonstrates why an external wrapper is insufficient, the exit-78 defect is repaired, and the operator contract is documented and owned.

recommendation.title: Keep orchestration external
recommendation.body: Have Lobster own the loopback activation listener and exec `openclaw gateway` after hydration, avoiding a permanent core protocol until a missing core capability is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans Gateway startup recovery, exposed-startup security, CLI startup, and daemon behavior, and the PR timeline shows direct interest.
